5.0 I have heard Sh. R.D.Goel, Advocate for appellants and Sh. Anil, Ld. Chief Public Prosecutor for the State and have perused the record carefully.

6.0 Admittedly, the sample food article Mater Masala was purchased from Sh.Ajay Gupta S/o Late Shri Ram Babu Gupta from the premises of M/s Rajasthan Bhujia Bhandar,F14/19, Model TownII, Delhi110009 on 02.07.2013.

It is also not in dispute that the Food Analyst vide his report dated 15.07.2013 reported the sample as misbranded as it violated Regulations 2.2.2.1, 2.2.2.4,
2.2.2.10, 2.3.1.5 & 2.3.2.1(a) of FSS(P&L)Regulation.
FSAT No.6/16 Ajay Gupta & Anr. Vs FSO
6.1 In view of the above, the Food Safety Officer filed a complaint/application under Rule 3.1.1(3) FSS Rules, 2011 before the Ld.ADM.
Notice of the same was issued to the appellants.
Perusal of the record shows that in response to the notice issued by Ld. ADM, Sh.Ajay Gupta, appellant no.1 put in appearance on 12.06.2014 and 25.06.2014.

The proceedings of 25.06.2014, read as under   "25.06.2014  .....FBO approached & he stated that he is not aware of  the provision of Food & Safety Act 2006 and he runs his  business since long period.
The officials for we  measurement had informed for preparing package in  present form & they have complied that instruction.
However  FBO pleaded guilty of the violation of
FSS  Act/Rule/Regulation
6.2 From the above, it is evident that the appellant expressed ignorance about the provisions of FSS Act and pleaded guilty.
None of the contentions as raised in the present appeal were raised before the Ld.ADM.

In view of these facts, it does not lie in the mouth of the appellant to now plead that the Ld.ADM did not consider his submissions/follow the procedure prescribed under the Act.

sentences.text: The appellants have contended that as required under Section 38(7) FSS Act, no independent witness was joined at the time of lifting of sample.
Perusal of the record shows that the Raid Report mentions at serial no.3 that attempts were made to include public witness but none agreed.
Even in the application under Rule 3.1.1(3) FSS Rules, filed by the Food Safety Officer before the Ld.
ADM mentions that the Food Safety Officer tried to associate public witnesses in the proceedings but none came forward.
He then requested, Ms.Usha Kiran, Food Safety Officer to join the sample proceedings as a witness, to which she agreed.
In view of these facts, it is apparent that due effort was made by the FSO to join a public witness but none agreed.
In view of the same, the judgments relied upon by the appellants are of no help in the instant case.

7.2 It is further contended by the appellants that the Ld.ADM failed to appreciate that the rule 2.4.2(1) of FSS Rules,
which requires that the Food Analyst shall compare the seals on the container and the outer cover with specimen impression of seal FSAT No.6/16 Ajay Gupta & Anr. Vs FSO   received separately and shall note the condition of the seal thereon,
was not complied with by the Food Analyst.

Let me refer to the Food Analyst report's relevant portion of which read as under: 
 "....
 The condition of seals on the con  outer covering on receipt was as follows :
 seals were intact & identical to the specimen impression of  the seal received from Food Safety Officer.
7.2.1 From the above it is apparent that the Food Analyst had recorded categoric observation that the seals were found intact and identical to the specimen impression of seal received from the FSO.
Thus, there is no force in the appellants' contention.

Accordingly,
the case law relied upon by him has no applicability in the present case.

7.3 Another ground on which the impugned order has been challenged is that the appellant no.2 has nothing to do with the business of the shop, although she is shown as the proprietor of the shop in the Rent Deed ; and that she was not even present at the time of purchase of samples.
This averment is wrong to the knowledge of the appellants themselves and reflect their falsehood.

7.4 It is also contended that the Ld. ADM did not appreciate that the sanction given by Designated Officer is bad in law.
However, no specific submission has been made either in the appeal or during oral arguments, as to how the same suffers from non application of mind and is bad.
The appellants could not point out any discrepancy in the sanction on record.
It is apparent that this FSAT No.6/16 Ajay Gupta & Anr. Vs FSO   contention has also been raised only for the sake of taking up some plea.

7.5 The appellants have taken yet another plea to challenge the impugned order.

That is, the Ld. ADM did not appreciate that "the sample commodity was taken from the tray by the FSO but that were taken out from the cardboard container same was to be supplied in the wholesale packages and all the legal formalities of label were complied with on the outer portion of the cardboard."
From the plain reading of this contention it is seen that contradictory averments are made by the appellants.

On one hand,
the appellants have contended that the sample commodity was taken from the tray and on the other hand, it is submitted that it was taken out from the cardboard container, in which the packets were kept for wholesale supply.
It is also pleaded that all the legal formalities were met on the label put on that cardboard container.
As already noted above, no such plea was raised by the appellants before the Ld.ADM.
Rather, the appellant no.1 expressed ignorance of law and pleaded guilty.
